recommendation: Purge the named-equipment catalog in two passes rather than one, because the catalog is load-bearing in ways its own prose denies. PASS ONE relocates before anything is deleted: the seven weapon properties become a menu a player selects when taking a kit Armament option; the Armament line gains an option that holds two weapons, since the combat chapter's procedure requires the Light property on an off-hand weapon and no current option can produce one; the nine class starting kits resolve to categories instead of 43 named entries; and the armour slot values and gear-table note rules land on the kit lines that price them. PASS TWO deletes the five named tables, de-registers them from the glossary and reference-sheet lookup surfaces, and repairs the six items the tables were silently propping up. Do not begin pass two before pass one lands: deleting first removes play rather than clutter.
rationale: All three topics reached the round cap contested, so the three sealed rulings carry the decision. The residue is real but smaller than the refuting side claimed: homonym correction removes a third of the apparent property burden (armour-class Light, the Human ancestry trait Versatile, monster Light Sensitivity), which leaves every property except Versatile with a genuine consumer. The kit's incompleteness is not in dispute and is structural: one select, five options, one shield. The catalogue's blast radius is measured rather than asserted - 400 named-item lines across the nine files and 77 table rows - so the migration is bounded work, not open-ended.

resolved.outcome: The kit model is not a complete replacement as written. Armament is a single select of five options and only one of them carries a shield, so a two-weapon build cannot be created even though the combat chapter defines the procedure and gates it on the Light property. Four of the nine class starting kits issue a second weapon. The named tables must not be deleted before a two-weapon option exists in the kit.

The residue is not wholesale and not negligible. Every weapon property except Versatile has a consumer, but the consumer set is far smaller than raw greps suggest because of homonyms. Versatile is decorative and may be retired. Finesse, Light, Loading, Thrown, Reach and Two-Handed must be relocated to the kit and card layer before their definitions are removed. Armour slots are item-level values that no per-class rule reproduces, so they survive only as a kit value or an explicit per-class figure.

The catalogue's consumers are enumerable and the blast radius is measured: 400 named-item lines across the nine files, 644 name occurrences, 77 table rows. Six defects must be repaired in the same pass, including the Plate 3 Armor entry requirement that no armour table supports, the Stealth-column promise that resolves to nothing, and the reference-sheet reprint that has silently diverged from the equipment chapter.

dissent.position: Round 2 abandoned the blanket refute and argued deletion-as-drafted holds for the weapons table and its reprint: the bestiary's weapon-labelled attack lines each print their own damage row and five name weapons with no catalog row at all, so that consumer is not a consumer; and the property burden shrinks because the two-slot rule already exists as a category rule and the off-hand tag has no procedure. Recorded, and partially accepted: the shrunk property burden is why Versatile is retired, but the two-weapon procedure the contrarian looked for sits outside the nine-file source set and does exist.
